topics.topic: Allowed base-URL forms, URL joining, and Host representation
questions: Are userinfo, query, fragment, non-root paths, percent escapes, Unicode hosts, IPv6 zone identifiers and trailing path segments allowed in `api_base_url`, and how are they joined and represented in `Host`?

Are user information, query, fragment, non-root base paths, percent-encoded separators, multiple trailing slashes, IPv6 zone identifiers, and other URL components permitted, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the `Host` header?
Which components may `api_base_url` contain, and exactly how are its existing path and authority converted into the final URL and Host header?

quotes:
one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none
judgement.why: The quoted base-URL rule is unchanged, and the change did not make its unspecified component handling matter.

topics.topic: Canonical multipart serialization and port-name encoding
questions: What exact multipart byte serialization must every implementation produce?
Which port names are permitted in multipart bindings, or how are quotes, backslashes, CR/LF and non-ASCII characters escaped?
Which port names are legal in multipart bindings, how are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII text and control characters encoded or refused, and what exact delimiter and CRLF framing is sent?
Which port names are legal in multipart requests, or how are arbitrary names escaped without changing their identity?

quotes:
The body is described as the JSON body's bytes, or for
   `multipart/form-data` as the parts in order, each as its name, filename when
   present, media type and the SHA-256 of its content, so the boundary is not
   part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.
judgement.why: The multipart-description passage is unchanged, and the change did not create the missing serialization or port-name rules.

topics.topic: Completeness rules for TrialCase input and expected-output maps
questions: Are missing inputs, extra inputs, and duplicate input names refused, and in what order relative to the listed per-port checks?
Does a present expected-output set assert all outputs or may it assert only a subset, and how are missing or extra expected-output names handled?
When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it specify only a subset?
Must trial inputs contain exactly all contract inputs, and when expected_outputs is present must it contain exactly all contract outputs?

quotes:
Either
   way it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input
   ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports, and every
   value is within `stored_value_bytes_max` and every file within
   `trial_fixture_bytes_max` — the first failing condition in this order is
   named, ports taken in name order and, for one port, presence, carriage,
   schema, then size.
judgement.why: These trial-case requirements are unchanged, and the change did not make map completeness newly consequential.

topics.topic: Durable representation of mapped-node aggregate outputs and many-file list metadata
questions: Where are a non-empty mapped node's collected outputs and their list class recorded when there is no aggregate NodeExecution?
Which record owns or names the collected `many` output of a non-empty mapped node, and do element records name individual outputs, the aggregate output, or both?
Which record durably names a mapped node's aggregate outputs when a non-empty map has no node-level NodeExecution?
Where are the order and disclosure class of a many-file list, especially an empty list, represented durably?

judgement.divergence: One implementer stores the aggregate list and its class in the last element's NodeExecution, while another records only per-element outputs and reconstructs or stores the aggregate only in downstream records; owner and agent trace readers, disclosure handling, and restart recovery observe different durable outputs.
judgement.why: The texts require a durable aggregate reference but do not identify an owning record for a non-empty map or define the list-level metadata representation.

topics.topic: Filesystem access allowed to function code
questions: May user code itself read arbitrary runtime files and read or write arbitrary exchange-directory paths, or are those locations accessible only to the runner?
Which runtime and exchange-directory paths, if any, may agent code itself enumerate, read, create, modify, or delete?
Exactly which filesystem operations may function code perform inside the exchange directory and runtime?

quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
judgement.why: The filesystem restriction is unchanged, and the change did not affect access by user code to runtime or exchange-directory paths.

topics.topic: Sandbox resource-limit accounting and detection
questions: What exact quantity is limited for sandbox scratch space and at what point is a limit considered hit?

What counts toward each limit, including interpreter and runner memory, the initial input files, deleted or overwritten scratch bytes, child processes, and transient output files, and how is a caught or indirectly observed limit hit distinguished from a crash?
What observable event proves that memory, process-count or scratch limits were hit, and how is a caught limit failure classified?
Which processes count against `process_count`, and at what instant is the count measured?

quotes:
ResourceBounds M04 are enforced from outside the environment with `setrlimit`
   (address space, processes) and the parent's own wall deadline and output
   count.
judgement.why: The resource-enforcement passage is unchanged, and the change did not introduce the unresolved accounting or detection choices.

topics.topic: Data-directory ownership, file-type, permission, and recursion requirements
questions: What exact filesystem ownership and permission conditions pass the startup check for directories and files?
What exact ownership, file-type and permission conditions define “private,” and are they checked recursively for every existing directory and file?

quotes: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
judgement.why: The privacy requirement is unchanged, and the change did not make its ownership, permission, file-type, ACL, hard-link, or recursion criteria matter.

topics.topic: Determining loopback eligibility for plain HTTP
questions: How is loopback status determined, especially for `localhost`, IPv6 forms and hostnames with changing or mixed DNS results?
Does this mean only a literal loopback IP address, or also a hostname that resolves to loopback, and how are mixed or changing DNS answers handled?

quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
judgement.why: The loopback exception is unchanged, and the change did not affect how a host is classified as loopback.

topics.topic: Handling and limits of sandbox stdout and stderr
questions: What happens when function code writes unbounded stdout or stderr: is it discarded through a bounded sink, counted against a limit, or allowed to block the process?
Where do stdout and stderr go, what bounds apply to them, and can excessive output change the execution outcome?

quotes: Nothing the code prints or raises is interpreted by the kernel.
judgement.why: The stdout and stderr rule is unchanged, and the change did not create the missing sink, bounding, or blocking behavior.

topics.topic: Precedence of invalid function output versus output-size limits
questions: How is output size determined for an invalid or non-serializable return, and which outcome wins when it is also extremely large?
How is output size evaluated when the return value is malformed or contains a value that cannot be represented as canonical JSON, and which outcome wins?

quotes:
The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every
   `value` output and the bytes of every `file` output of the one call of `run` —
   for a `many` file output, the sum of its elements' bytes.
judgement.why: The output-size definition is unchanged, and the change did not make sizing non-canonical or malformed Python return values newly relevant.

topics.topic: Scope of the sandbox clock prohibition
questions: Are all unlisted ways of observing time forbidden, or are they permitted despite the no-clock rule?
Does the closed trap list define the allowed behavior, or must every standard-library route to clock or elapsed-time information be denied?

quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The closed trap-list rule is unchanged, and the change did not affect the scope of the no-clock prohibition.

topics.topic: Spool deduplication, ownership, and crash-safe release or deletion
questions: Are equal spool bytes deduplicated across attempts or runs, and if so how are ownership, reference counts and deletion handled?
What happens if deletion partly succeeds, fails, or the process crashes between deleting files and recording release or final run state?

quotes:
A `failed` run keeps its spool until the owner or an agent releases it; release
   removes the files, records who and when, and is refused for a run that is not
   `failed` or was already released (K-10).
judgement.why: The deduplication and release passages are unchanged, and the change did not create the unresolved ownership, reference-counting, or partial-deletion behavior.

topics.topic: Whether multipart serialization and boundary changes invalidate approval
questions: Does changing the actual multipart boundary void an approval?
Does changing multipart serialization or its boundary invalidate an approval, or does approval intentionally cover only the logical parts?

quotes:
The body is described as the JSON body's bytes, or for
   `multipart/form-data` as the parts in order, each as its name, filename when
   present, media type and the SHA-256 of its content, so the boundary is not
   part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.
judgement.why: The logical multipart request-description rule is unchanged, and the change did not affect whether wire-level boundary or serialization differences void approval.

topics.topic: Atomicity and repair of admission verdict plus automatic activation
questions: Can an admitted verdict exist without its required automatic activation after a crash, and what operation repairs that state?

topics.topic: Byte representation covered by file digests
questions: Is a file digest SHA-256 of the raw file bytes, a canonical JSON encoding of those bytes, or another representation?

topics.topic: Canonical JSON HTTP request serialization
questions: What exact JSON serialization, member order, UTF-8 escaping, and number formatting are used for the HTTP body?

topics.topic: Conversion of malformed HTTP error bytes into bounded failure detail
questions: How are non-UTF-8 bytes, NULs, control characters, and a truncation point inside a multibyte sequence converted to bounded failure-detail text?

topics.topic: Definition of a control character
questions: Does `control character` mean ASCII C0 and DEL, C1 controls too, or every Unicode character in category `Cc`?

topics.topic: Deterministic ordering of equal-key FlowVersion facts
questions: How are edges or constants ordered when those stated keys are equal but their guards, values, or other facts differ, both for hashing and for choosing the first failure?

topics.topic: Disclosure class for executions with no recorded values
questions: What disclosure class has a zero-input execution with no recorded output, such as a crashing zero-input function or a no-input/no-output operation?

topics.topic: Equality semantics for guard values
questions: How are guard values compared, especially numbers such as 1 and 1.0 and structured values?

topics.topic: Exact sandbox audit events and prohibited operations
questions: What exact Python audit-event names, arguments, path operations, imports, and low-level process APIs constitute each prohibited category?

topics.topic: Handling nondeterministic function results during admission
questions: What happens if repeated executions of the same implementation and case produce different outputs or outcomes?

topics.topic: Handling of encoded HTTP response bodies
questions: Is an encoded response rejected, decoded before size and schema checks, or treated as raw response bytes?

topics.topic: Legal HTTP header characters and wire encoding
questions: Which characters are legal in required and credential header values, and how are non-ASCII values encoded on the wire?

topics.topic: Meaning and validation of file-port value schemas
questions: What does a file port's `value_schema` describe, and how does the kernel decide that file bytes or a file fixture fit it without inspecting content?

topics.topic: Media-type syntax, identity, and comparison normalization
questions: May declared media types contain parameters or mixed case, and are edge equality, stored identity and HTTP response matching textual or normalized comparisons?

topics.topic: OperationBinding schema validation and check ordering
questions: Must binding port schemas be validated against the same supported JSON Schema subset as contract ports, and where does that check occur in A08 rule 5's order?

topics.topic: Ordering of records written within one transaction
questions: How are distinct records written in the same transaction ordered relative to one another?

topics.topic: Outcome precedence for incomplete HTTP response bodies
questions: If a valid final status and headers arrive but the body times out, resets, or ends prematurely, does the transport-failure row win or does the received status determine the outcome?

topics.topic: Outcome when the selected manifest instance is absent
questions: Does a nonexistent selected instance count as no selection, an invalid installation that stops startup, or a distinct proposal/send failure?

topics.topic: Privacy-safe sanitization of stored failure details
questions: May `failure_detail` contain business or personal payload text, and if not, what deterministic sanitization replaces it before storage?

topics.topic: Release-ceiling version applied to existing and recovered objects
questions: Which ceiling version applies to existing flows, trial cases, active runs and recovered runs after a release upgrade?

topics.topic: Release-pinned Python, sandbox, and operating-system dependencies
questions: Which exact CPython patch release, bubblewrap version, operating-system facilities and compatibility checks define release v1 behavior?

topics.topic: Retrieval and validation of manifest bytes at a revision
questions: How does the kernel obtain bytes at a revision, how is the revision validated, and what happens when the working tree differs or the revision is unavailable?

topics.topic: Retry eligibility after service-unreachable mapped attempts
questions: Is `service_unreachable` a concluded attempt but not a concluded element, and what exact statuses make an element ineligible for another attempt?

topics.topic: Run pinning to an exact FlowActivation
questions: Which exact FlowActivation does a run pin, and where is that identity recorded so a later reactivation of the same version cannot change the authority of a draft-write?

topics.topic: Stable pagination order and cursor behavior under status changes
questions: Does updating an entity's status move it in list order, and which position is used by continuation tokens?
What happens when a record above the continuation cursor changes from nonmatching to matching, or a record below it changes in the opposite direction?

topics.topic: Treatment and reuse of interrupted admission executions
questions: Are partial admission TrialExecutions retained as ordinary evidence, removed, or resumed, and does the next submission reuse any of them?

topics.topic: Use and comparison of file outputs as guards
questions: Can a `file` output be a guard port, and if so how is its content compared?

topics.topic: Validity of cached admission verdicts after sandbox dependency upgrades
questions: After an upgrade changes Python or sandbox dependencies, may an implementation continue running under its old cached admission verdict?

topics.topic: Validity of empty node IDs and endpoint identity
questions: May a real node have the empty `node_id`, and if not, where is that composition refusal ordered?
